paragraphs: AGNC Investment Corp. ("AGNC," the "Company," "we," "us" and "our") was organized on January 7, 2008 and commenced operations on May 20, 2008 following the completion of our initial public offering. Our common stock is traded on The Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "AGNC."

We are a leading provider of private capital to the U.S. housing market, enhancing liquidity in the residential real estate mortgage markets and, in turn, facilitating home ownership in the U.S. We invest primarily in Agency residential mortgage-backed securities ("Agency RMBS") on a leveraged basis. These investments consist of residential mortgage pass-through securities and collateralized mortgage obligations for which the principal and interest payments are guaranteed by a U.S. Government-sponsored enterprise, such as the Federal National Mortgage Association ("Fannie Mae") and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation ("Freddie Mac," and together with Fannie Mae, the "GSEs"), or by a U.S. Government agency, such as the Government National Mortgage Association ("Ginnie Mae").

We operate to qualify to be taxed as a real estate investment trust ("REIT") under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Internal Revenue Code"). As a REIT, we are required to distribute annually 90% of our taxable income, and we will generally not be subject to U.S. federal or state corporate income tax to the extent that we distribute all our annual taxable income to our stockholders on a timely basis. It is our intention to distribute 100% of our taxable income within the time limits prescribed by the Internal Revenue Code, which may extend into the subsequent taxable year.

We are internally managed with the principal objective of generating favorable long-term stockholder returns with a substantial yield component. We generate income from the interest earned on our investments, net of associated borrowing and hedging costs, and net realized gains and losses on our investment and hedging activities. We fund our investments primarily through collateralized borrowings structured as repurchase agreements.

We employ an active management strategy that is dynamic and responsive to evolving market conditions. The composition of our portfolio and our investment, funding, and hedging strategies are tailored to reflect our analysis of market conditions and the relative values of available options. Our portfolio management philosophy is based upon the following core objectives:
•deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns for our stockholders primarily through monthly dividend distributions;
•maintain an investment portfolio consisting predominantly of Agency RMBS; •manage financing, interest rate, prepayment, extension and credit risks;
•remain exempt from the requirements of the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "Investment Company Act").

Asset selection is a central component of our overall investment approach. Our investments consist predominantly of Agency RMBS which, in addition to carrying a GSE or U.S. Government guarantee against loss of principal, are considered a cornerstone of the U.S. financial system. The $9 trillion Agency market plays a vital role in providing liquidity to homeowners and prospective homeowners to purchase or refinance homes. We may also invest in Agency multifamily mortgage-backed securities ("Agency multifamily MBS") that are similarly guaranteed by a GSE and in other assets related to the housing, mortgage, or real estate markets that are not guaranteed by a GSE or a U.S. Government agency (collectively referred to as "non-Agency MBS").

Our team of investment professionals has decades of experience investing in Agency RMBS and our other targeted investments. Our asset selection process involves assessing relative risk-return profiles against the backdrop of broader market conditions. Utilizing sophisticated modeling techniques, we identify assets with favorable underlying loan characteristics with the objective of optimizing returns over the life of the investment.

•Agency Residential Mortgage-Backed Securities. Agency RMBS consist of pass-through certificates representing interests in "pools" of mortgage loans secured by residential real property. Monthly payments of principal and interest made by the individual borrowers on the mortgage loans underlying the pools are in effect "passed through" to the security holders, after deducting guarantee and servicer fees. In general, mortgage pass-through certificates

distribute cash flows from the underlying collateral on a pro rata basis among the security holders. Security holders also receive guarantor advances of principal and interest for delinquent loans in the mortgage pools. We may also invest in Agency collateralized mortgage obligations ("CMOs"), which are structured instruments backed by a pool of Agency RMBS.

•To-Be-Announced Forward Contracts ("TBAs"). TBAs are forward contracts to purchase or sell Agency RMBS in the TBA market. TBA contracts specify the coupon rate, issuer, term and face value of the bonds to be delivered, with the actual bonds to be delivered only identified shortly before the TBA settlement date.

•Agency Multifamily Mortgage-Backed Securities. Agency multifamily MBS consist of securities backed by one or more mortgage loans secured by one or more multifamily properties that benefit from a GSE guarantee of timely payment of principal and interest. Our investments in Agency multifamily securities primarily consist of securities issued under Fannie Mae's Delegated Underwriting and Servicing ("DUS") program, which are generally backed by a single mortgage loan secured by a single property and include lender risk-sharing.

headings: Risks Related to Our Investment and Portfolio Management Activities
Spread risk is inherent to our business as a levered investor in Agency RMBS.
Interest rate and spread volatility represent significant risks to our business, potentially affecting our liquidity, increasing our costs, and impacting our ability to manage risks effectively.
The participation of the Fed and other government-related entities in the Agency mortgage market could have an adverse effect on our Agency RMBS investments.
Our active portfolio management strategy may expose us to greater losses and lower returns than compared to passive strategies.
A decline in the fair value of our assets may adversely affect our financial condition and make it costlier to finance our assets.
Changes in prepayment rates may adversely affect the return on our investments.

Prepayment rates are difficult to predict, and market conditions and other factors impacting mortgage origination channels may disrupt the historical correlation between interest rate changes and prepayment trends.
The analytical models and third-party data that we rely on to manage our portfolio and conduct our business objectives may be incorrect, misleading or incomplete.
The fair value of our investments may not be readily determinable or may be materially different from the value that we ultimately realize upon their disposal.
The mortgage loans referenced by our CRT securities or that underlie our non-Agency securities may be or could become subject to delinquency or foreclosure, which could result in investment losses.
Private mortgage insurance may not cover losses on loans referenced by our CRT securities and underlying our non-Agency RMBS.
Changes in credit spreads may adversely affect our profitability.
We may be unable to acquire desirable investments due to competition, a reduction in the supply of new production Agency RMBS having the specific attributes we seek, and other factors.
We may change our targeted investments, investment guidelines and other operational policies without stockholder consent.
Risks Related to Our Financing and Hedging Activities
Our strategy involves the use of significant leverage, which increases the risk that we may incur substantial losses.
We may be unable to procure or renew funding on favorable terms, or at all.
Our borrowing costs may increase at a faster pace than the yield on our investments.

It may be uneconomical to roll our TBA dollar roll transactions, which could require us to take physical delivery of the underlying securities and fund our obligations with cash or other financing sources.
Our funding and derivative agreements subject us to margin calls that could result in defaults and force us to sell assets under adverse market conditions or through foreclosure.
Changes to FICC margin requirements could limit our ability to enter tri-party repo transactions with the FICC's GCF Repo service and TBA transactions with the FICC's MBSD
Our repurchase agreements and agreements governing certain derivative instruments may contain financial and non-financial covenants subjecting us to the risk of default.
Our rights under repurchase and derivative agreements in the event of bankruptcy or insolvency may be limited.
Our funding and derivative agreement counterparties may not fulfill their obligations to us when due.
Our hedging strategies may be ineffective.
Risks Related to Our Business Operations
Our executive officers and other key personnel are critical to our success and the loss of any executive officer or key employee may materially adversely affect our business.
The use of artificial intelligence by us or our third-party vendors could expose us to additional risks.
Risks Related to Our Taxation as a REIT
Our failure to qualify as a REIT would have adverse tax consequences.
REIT distribution requirements could adversely affect our ability to execute our business plan.
We may choose to pay dividends in our own stock, in which case stockholders may be required to pay income taxes in excess of cash dividends received.
Even if we remain qualified as a REIT, we may face other tax liabilities that reduce our cash flow.
Complying with REIT requirements may cause us to liquidate or forgo attractive investment opportunities.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks described below and all other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our annual consolidated financial statements and the related notes thereto before deciding to purchase our securities. Any of the following risks could materially affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. If that happens, the trading price of our securities could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or not presently deemed material by us, may also impair our operations and performance. Our risk factors discussed below are classified among:
•risks related to our investment and portfolio management activities; •risks related to our financing and hedging activities;
•risks related to our business operations; •legislative and regulatory risks; and

When the differential (or "spread") between the market yield on our assets and our interest rate hedges widens, our tangible net book value will typically decline, a dynamic we refer to as "spread risk." As a levered investor primarily in fixed-rate Agency RMBS, spread risk is an inherent component of our business. Although we use hedging instruments in an effort to protect against moves in interest rates, our hedges will typically not protect us against spread risk. Spreads may widen due to

numerous factors, including actual or expected monetary policy actions by U.S. and foreign central banks; legislative, regulatory or other administrative actions affecting the Agency RMBS market; changes in fiscal policy and rising federal budget deficits; increased market volatility; reduced market liquidity; higher Agency RMBS supply; and shifts in investor return requirements and sentiment.

Interest rate and spread volatility can materially and adversely impact our business, financial condition, and operating results. Elevated volatility amplifies market risks that affect the value of our assets and liabilities and can reduce earnings stability. Increased volatility also heightens our exposure to margin calls, including higher risk-based margin requirements, which may require us to post additional collateral, thereby reducing our unencumbered cash and other liquid assets (or "unencumbered liquidity") and thus limiting resources available for operational needs and further margin obligations.

paragraphs: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") is designed to provide a reader of AGNC Investment Corp.'s consolidated financial statements with a narrative from the perspective of management and should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our MD&A is presented in the following sections:
•Executive Overview •Financial Condition •Summary of Critical Accounting Estimates •Results of Operations
•Liquidity and Capital Resources •Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements •Forward-Looking Statements
•Website and Social Media Disclosure EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW

We are a leading provider of private capital to the U.S. housing market, enhancing liquidity in the residential real estate mortgage markets and, in turn, facilitating home ownership in the U.S. We invest primarily in Agency RMBS on a leveraged basis. These investments consist of residential mortgage pass-through securities and collateralized mortgage obligations for which the principal and interest payments are guaranteed by a U.S. Government-sponsored enterprise, such as Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, or by a U.S. Government agency, such as Ginnie Mae. We may also invest in Agency multifamily MBS that are similarly guaranteed by a GSE and in other assets related to the housing, mortgage or real estate markets that are not guaranteed by a GSE or U.S. Government agency.

We are internally managed with the principal objective of generating favorable long-term stockholder returns with a substantial yield component. We generate income from the interest earned on our investments, net of associated borrowing and hedging costs, and net realized gains and losses on our investment and hedging activities. We fund our investments primarily through collateralized borrowings structured as repurchase agreements. We operate in a manner to qualify to be taxed as a REIT under the Internal Revenue Code.

We employ an active management strategy that is dynamic and responsive to evolving market conditions. The composition of our portfolio and our investment, funding, and hedging strategies are tailored to reflect our analysis of market conditions and the relative values of available options. Market conditions are influenced by a variety of factors, including interest rates, prepayment expectations, liquidity, housing prices, unemployment rates, general economic conditions, government participation in the mortgage market, regulations and relative returns on other assets.

Agency RMBS outperformed domestic fixed income alternatives in 2025, and this favorable asset class performance, coupled with AGNC's active portfolio management strategies, drove AGNC's best-in-class economic return for the year.1 In 2025, the Bloomberg US Mortgage Backed Securities Index (the "Agency MBS Index"), which represents the entire Agency RMBS market, generated a total return of 8.6% for the year, its best annual performance since 2002. Also notable, given the similar credit profile, the Agency MBS Index outperformed the Bloomberg US Treasury Index by 2.3 percentage points, or 36%.
A number of factors that materialized over the course of the year catalyzed the strong performance of Agency RMBS, including:

•The Federal Reserve (the "Fed") shifted monetary policy toward lower short-term interest rates and greater accommodation, which contributed to the positive performance of all domestic fixed income asset classes.
•Greater fiscal policy clarity and the stable supply outlook for U.S. Treasury securities contributed to reduced interest rate volatility.

•Improved conditions in short-term funding markets, particularly late in the year, benefited Agency RMBS, as the Fed announced an expansion of its balance sheet through reserve management purchases of short-term Treasury bills, as well as other actions that improved the functionality and accessibility of its Standing Repo Program.
•The Administration articulated a framework for GSE reform that focused on reducing Agency mortgage spreads, maintaining mortgage market stability, and improving housing affordability.

Collectively, these factors—along with sizable Agency MBS purchases by the GSEs later in the year—led to lower Agency RMBS spread volatility, tighter mortgage spreads to benchmark rates, and the outperformance of Agency RMBS relative to other fixed income asset classes.

paragraphs: AGNC Investment Corp. ("AGNC," the "Company," "we," "us" and "our") 於 2008 年 1 月 7 日成立，並於 2008 年 5 月 20 日開始營運，此為我們首次公開發行後完成。本公司普通股於納斯達克全球選選市場交易，代碼為 "AGNC"。

本公司為美國住宅房地產抵押貸款市場提供私人資本的主要供應商，提升住宅不動產抵押貸款市場的流動性，進而促進美國的房屋擁有率。我們主要以槓桿方式投資於美國住宅抵押貸款支持證券（"Agency RMBS"）。這些投資包括住宅抵押貸款過手證券與擔保抵押貸款憑證，其本金與利息支付由美國政府支持企業，例如美國房屋貸款公司（"Fannie Mae"）與美國房屋貸款抵押公司（"Freddie Mac"，與 Fannie Mae 合稱 "GSEs"），或由美國政府機構，例如美國住宅抵押貸款公司（"Ginnie Mae"）所擔保。
本公司運作目標為符合美國 1986 年所得稅法（"Internal Revenue Code"）的規定，被認定為不動產投資信託（"REIT"）。作為 REIT，本公司每年必須分配 90% 的應稅所得，且在符合時間條件下，本公司一般不會被課徵美國聯邦或州級公司所得稅。本公司意圖在所得稅法所規定的時間內，將 100% 的應稅所得分配給股東，此時間可能延長至下一年度的課稅期間。
本公司為內部管理，主要目標為為股東產生有利的長期投資回報，並具有相當的收益組成。本公司收入來自投資所產生的利息，扣除相關借款與避險成本，以及投資與避險活動的淨實現損益。本公司主要透過擔保借款結構的回購協議來資助投資。
本公司採用積極的管理策略，此策略靈活且能因應市場條件的變化。投資組合的組成與投資、資金與避險策略均根據市場條件與可選方案的相對價值進行調整。本公司投資組合管理的理念基於以下核心目標：
•為股東提供具吸引力的風險調整後回報，主要透過每月股息發放；
•維持主要由 Agency RMBS 組成的投資組合；•管理融資、利率、提前償還、延長與信用風險；
•保持免於符合 1940 年投資公司法（"Investment Company Act"）的規定。

資產選擇是我們整體投資策略的核心零組件。我們的投資主要由機構 RMBS 組成，除了具有 GSE 或美國政府對本金損失的擔保外，也被視為美國金融體系的基石。規模達 9 兆美元的機構市場在提供流動性給房東及潛在房東購屋或重貸方面扮演關鍵角色。我們也可能投資於機構多戶房貸-backed 投資信託（"機構多戶 MBS"），這些投資信託同樣由 GSE 擔保，並投資其他與住宅、房貸或不動產市場相關的資產，這些資產並未由 GSE 或美國政府機構擔保（ collectively referred to as "non-Agency MBS"）。
我們的投資專業團隊擁有數十年投資機構 RMBS 及其他目標資產的經驗。我們的資產選擇流程涉及在總體經濟條件的背景下評估相對風險回報特性。透過運用先進的建模技術，我們識別出具有優良貸款特性的資產，以達到投資壽命內優化回報的目標。
•機構住宅房貸-backed 投資信託。機構 RMBS 為代表對 "房貸貸款池" 之權益的過手證券，這些貸款池由住宅不動產抵押貸款所組成。個別借款人對其房貸貸款所支付的本金與利息，在扣除擔保與服務費後，會「過手」至證券持有人。一般而言，房貸過手證券
會根據基礎抵押貸款的資產，在證券持有人之間按比例分配現金流。證券持有人也會收到擔保人對逾期貸款本金與利息的預付。我們也可能投資於機構抵押貸款過手證券（"CMOs"），這些為由機構 RMBS 構成的結構化工具。
•待公告前進合約（"TBAs"）。TBAs 為在 TBA 市場上買入或賣出機構 RMBS 的遠期合約。TBA 合約會指定將交付的債券的票息率、發行者、期限及面值，實際交付的債券僅在 TBA 交割日臨近時才會確定。
•機構多戶房貸-backed 投資信託。機構多戶 MBS 為由一個或多個抵押貸款所支持的證券，這些抵押貸款由一個或多個多戶不動產所組成，並受益於 GSE 對本金與利息按時支付的擔保。我們在機構多戶證券上的投資主要為根據房利美（Fannie Mae）的委託審核與服務（"DUS"）計劃所發行的證券，這些證券通常由單一抵押貸款所支持，並包含貸款人風險共擔。

我們是美國住宅不動產抵押貸款市場之主要私人資本供應者，提升住宅不動產抵押貸款市場之流動性，進而促進美國住宅擁有率。我們主要以槓桿方式投資於由美國政府機構所擔保之房貸證券（Agency RMBS）。這些投資包括住宅抵押貸款過手證券與擔保抵押貸款證券，其本金與利息支付由美國政府機構所擔保，例如房利美（Fannie Mae）與房地美（Freddie Mac），或由美國政府機構所擔保，例如吉利美（Ginnie Mae）。我們也可能投資於由GSE所擔保之房貸證券，以及與住宅、房貸或不動產市場相關之其他資產，這些資產並未由GSE或美國政府機構擔保。
我們為內部管理，主要目標為產生有利之長期股東回報，並具有顯著之收益組成。我們的收入來自於投資所產生之利息收入，扣除相關借款與避險成本，以及投資與避險活動之淨實現損益。我們主要透過結構為回購協議之擔保借款來資助投資。我們以符合美國內政部稅收法規之REIT（不動產投資信託）方式運作。
我們採用積極之管理策略，並能根據市場變動進行靈活調整。我們投資組合之組成以及投資、資金與避險策略，均根據我們對市場條件與可用選項之相對價值之分析進行調整。市場條件受多種因素影響，包括利率、預付款預期、流動性、住宅價格、失業率、總體經濟狀況、政府在房貸市場之參與程度、規範以及其他資產之相對報酬率。

2025年，Agency RMBS表現優於國內固定收益替代方案，此優良資產類別表現，加上AGNC積極之投資組合管理策略，驅動AGNC在該年度取得業界最佳之經濟回報。1 2025年，彭博美國房貸證券指數（"Agency MBS指數"），代表整個Agency RMBS市場，產生年總回報率為8.6%，為自2002年以來最佳年度表現。此外，考慮到相似之信用風險，Agency MBS指數表現優於彭博美國國庫券指數2.3個百分點，或36%。
多項因素在本年度內實現，促使代理機構RMBS表現強勁，包括：
• 聯邦儲備系統（the "Fed"）轉向較低的短期利率與較為寬鬆的貨幣政策，這有助於所有國內固定收益資產類別的正面表現。
• 更明確的財政政策與美國國庫券供應展望穩定，導致利率波動減少。
• 短期融資市場條件改善，特別是在年尾，受益於代理機構RMBS，因聯邦儲備系統宣佈透過儲備管理購買短期國庫券來擴大其資產負債表，以及其他改善其常設回購計畫功能與可近性的措施。
• 政府提出了一套關於GSE改革的架構，重點在於降低代理機構房貸利差、維持房貸市場穩定，以及改善住宅 affordability。

collectively, these factors—along with sizable Agency MBS purchases by the GSEs later in the year—led to lower Agency RMBS spread volatility, tighter mortgage spreads to benchmark rates, and the outperformance of Agency RMBS relative to other fixed income asset classes.

headings: 與本公司投資及資產管理活動相關之風險
作為擔保品抵押貸款支持證券（Agency RMBS）之槓桿投資者，我們的業務本質上包含分散風險。
利率與利差波動對我們的業務構成重大風險，可能影響我們的流動性，增加我們的成本，並影響我們有效管理風險的能力。
聯邦儲備委員會（Fed）及其他政府相關機構參與擔保品抵押貸款支持證券市場，可能對我們的擔保品抵押貸款支持證券投資產生不利影響。
我們積極的資產管理策略可能使我們面臨較高之損失與較低之回報，與被動策略相比。
我們資產之公允價值下降可能對我們之財務狀況產生不利影響，並使我們資產之融資成本增加。
預付款率之變動可能對我們之投資回報產生不利影響。
預付款率難以預測，且市場條件及其他影響房貸發放渠道之因素，可能幹擾利率變動與預付款趨勢之間歷史相關性。
我們用來管理投資組合及執行業務目標的分析模型及第三方資料，可能不正確、誤導性或不完整。
我們投資的公允價值可能無法迅速確定，或與我們最終在處置時實現的價值有重大差異。
我們CRT證券所參考的或用以支撐我們非機構證券的抵押貸款，可能或可能成為違約或法拍，這可能會導致投資損失。
私人房貸保險可能不會涵蓋我們CRT證券所參考貸款或我們非機構RMBS所支撐貸款的損失。
信用 spreads 的變動可能對我們的獲利造成不利影響。
我們可能因競爭、新發行機構RMBS供應減少且具備我們所尋求特定屬性，以及其他因素，而無法取得理想投資。
我們可能在股東同意的情況下，改變我們的目標投資、投資指引及其他營運政策。
與我們融資及對沖活動相關的風險
本公司策略涉及使用大量槓桿，這會增加我們可能產生重大虧損的風險。
本公司可能無法以有利條件取得或續約資金，或根本無法取得。
本公司借款成本可能以快於投資回報率的幅度增加。
滾動TBA美元滾動交易可能不經濟，這可能會導致我們必須以實際交付基礎證券，並以現金或其他融資來源履行義務。
本公司資金及衍生品協議使我們面臨追繳保證金的風險，這可能會導致違約，並迫使我們在不利市場條件下出售資產或透過拍賣取得資產。
FICC保證金要求的變更可能會限制本公司與FICC的GCF Repo服務進行三方回購交易，以及與FICC的MBSD進行TBA交易的能力。
本公司回購協議及某些衍生工具協議可能包含財務及非財務契約條款，使我們面臨違約的風險。
本公司在破產或財務困難時根據回購及衍生品協議所擁有的權利可能受到限制。
本公司資金及衍生性商品協議之交易對手可能無法於到期時履行其對我們的義務。
本公司避險策略可能無法達到預期效果。
與本公司營運相關之風險
本公司高階主管及其他關鍵人員對本公司之成功至關重要，若失去任何高階主管或關鍵員工，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司或第三方供應商使用人工智慧，可能使本公司面臨額外風險。
與本公司作為REIT之稅務相關之風險
本公司若無法符合REIT之資格，將導致稅務上之不利後果。
REIT分紅要求可能影響本公司執行業務計畫之能力。
本公司可能選擇以本公司股票發放股息，此情況下股東可能需支付高於現金股息所收到金額的所得稅。
即使本公司持續符合REIT資格，仍可能面臨其他稅務負擔，進而降低本公司現金流。
符合REIT要求可能導致本公司出售或放棄具吸引力之投資機會。
paragraphs: 您應仔細審閱下列所列風險，以及本年度報告表10-K所包含的所有資訊，包括我們的年度合併財務報表及其相關附註，再決定是否購買本公司證券。任何下列風險都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大影響。如果發生這種情況，本公司證券的交易價格可能會下跌，您也可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所列的風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不具重大性，也可能影響我們的營運與表現。我們在下列所討論的風險因素，則分為：
•與我們投資及資產管理活動相關的風險；•與我們融資及避險活動相關的風險；
•與我們業務營運相關的風險；•立法與監管風險；以及
當我們資產市場報酬率與我們利率避險之間的差異（或稱為"利差"）擴大時，我們的實質淨書面價值通常會下降，這種現象我們稱為"利差風險"。作為主要投資於固定利率機構房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS）的槓桿投資者，利差風險是我們業務內在的一部分。儘管我們使用避險工具來試圖對抗利率變動，但我們的避險措施通常不會保護我們免受利差風險的影響。利差擴大的原因可能包括
許多因素，包括美國與外國央行實際或預期的貨幣政策行動；影響機構房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS）市場的立法、監管或其他行政措施；財政政策的變化與聯邦預算赤字增加；市場波動性增加；市場流動性下降；機構房貸支持證券（Agency RMBS）供應增加；以及投資者回報需求與情緒的變化。
利率與利差波動可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。高波動性會放大影響我們資產與負債價值的市場風險，並可能降低獲利的穩定性。增加的波動性也會提高我們的追繳保證金風險，包括更高的風險基準保證金要求，這可能會導致我們需要追加擔保品，從而減少我們的未設定抵押現金及其他流動資產（或稱為"未設定抵押流動性"），進而限制我們用於營運需求與進一步追繳保證金的資源。
